newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper to target $2,300 resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper to target $2,300 resistance.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper is expected to gravitate towards $2,300 resistance after a positive chart close on Friday and with Third Wednesday pricing seen later on Monday, traders and analysts said.
Aluminium should try to break through a ceiling of $1,585 a tonne, targeting next resistance at $1,600, they added.
COPPER -
Copper is expected to attack $2,300 after closing near its highs on Friday, then target $2,350.

"The close is constructive and, coupled with the oversold technical indicators pulling off the lows, suggests that further strength can be expected," said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff.

Third Wednesday pricing later on Monday should support prices, which have been hit by technical tightness recently. The cash/threes backwardation was indicated early on Monday at $145/55, about $15 wider than on Friday evening.
After the $2,300 area, prices should shoot up towards $2,350.
"With further nearby tightness expected to support the market, prices should target $2,350," broker Brandeis said.
Support was pegged at $2,250, the lows of Thursday and Friday, and just above that area based on a long-term uptrend line.
At 0835 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,292/95, up around $9 from Friday's late close.
ALUMINIUM -
Prices also scored a positive close on Friday and the 10-day moving average was looking to make a bullish cross above the 30-day average around $1,590.
That should help give the market enough steam to make a successful break above nearby resistance of $1,585 and go on to attack $1,600.
But the market would have to push above $1,620, the recent high hit on July 3, to signal that an uptrend was in place.
"To suggest the recent rally's continuation, we would then want to see the recent $1,620 peak negated," Squires said.
At 0835 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,588/91, up $8 from Friday's late close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
